basics.name: Yilin Liu
basics.label: Undergraduate Student
basics.summary: I am an undergraduate student at HKUST(GZ) majoring in Data Science and Big Data Technology, and was a visiting student at UC Berkeley in Fall 2025. My research interests lie broadly in efficient and scalable AI systems, especially for Large Language Models. I am interested in improving LLM efficiency across the stack, including high-quality data synthesis, mathematical reasoning, model compression, quantization, and system-level optimization.

projects.name: System-Algorithm Co-design for Efficient LLM Quantization
projects.summary: An ongoing research project on efficient LLM inference and model compression. The project aims to design accurate and efficient low-bit quantization methods through system-algorithm co-design, balancing model quality, memory efficiency, and runtime performance under practical hardware and system constraints.

projects.name: ClawMobile: Efficient and Reliable Smartphone-Native Agentic Systems
projects.summary: A recent research exploration on mobile agent systems at MBZUAI. I am investigating token efficiency, skill representation, and execution reliability in smartphone-native agentic systems, with an interest in making agent workflows more efficient and robust on real mobile environments.

projects.name: SynerMath: Multi-Agent Synthesis of High-Quality Mathematical Data for Efficient LLM Reasoning
projects.summary: SynerMath is a multi-agent framework for synthesizing compact yet high-fidelity mathematical question-answer corpora to improve LLM reasoning efficiently. As the second author and sole undergraduate contributor, I worked on literature survey, multi-agent pipeline design, and empirical evaluation across in-domain and out-of-domain mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

projects.name: Utilizing Chromoprotein Expression to Counteract Coral Bleaching
projects.summary: To address coral bleaching, this project designed a genetic circuit that conditionally expresses chromoproteins regulated by heat and light intensity, mimicking the protective effects of turbid waters and reducing the damage caused by high temperature and high light intensity to corals. As one of the main wet lab contributors, I contributed to the design of a key circuit part and conducted intensive wet lab experiments, covering protocol design, assay execution, and experimental documentation.
